intent.raw_query: Vietnam on $800, backpacking 10 days, street food and culture, April 2026

experiences.name: Hanoi Old Quarter Street Food Walk
experiences.description: Explore the bustling 36 streets of Hanoi's Old Quarter on foot, sampling iconic street foods like Bun Cha, Banh Mi, and Egg Coffee from local vendors. Stay in a hostel within the Old Quarter itself to maximize time and minimize travel. Since the flight arrives late on Day 1, this activity is perfectly suited for Day 2 morning when you are already rested and centrally located.

experiences.name: Hoi An Ancient Town Lantern Festival and Night Market
experiences.description: Wander through the UNESCO-listed Ancient Town of Hoi An, visit tailor shops, temples, and assembly halls by day, then experience the magical lantern-lit night market along the Thu Bon River. Book accommodation within the Ancient Town or on Tran Phu Street to walk everywhere without transport costs. Ideal for mid-trip when you have settled into the backpacking rhythm.

experiences.name: Hue Imperial Citadel and Local Com Hen Lunch
experiences.description: Spend a morning cycling around the Hue Imperial Citadel and royal tombs, then stop at a local eatery inside the citadel area for Com Hen, a signature Hue dish of baby clams on rice. Stay in a guesthouse on Hung Vuong Street near the citadel to avoid long commutes and make the most of the day after a morning arrival by train or bus from Hoi An.

experiences.name: Ho Chi Minh City Ben Thanh Market Street Food and Pham Ngu Lao Backpacker District
experiences.description: Dive into the vibrant street food scene around Ben Thanh Market, tasting Banh Xeo, Hu Tieu, and fresh sugarcane juice, then explore the nearby Pham Ngu Lao backpacker hub for budget bars and travel connections. Since the flight arrives after 20:00, book a hostel directly in Pham Ngu Lao so you can drop your bags and immediately join the lively night scene without wasting the late evening.
experiences.location: Pham Ngu Lao and Ben Thanh, Ho Chi Minh City

experiences.name: Ninh Binh Tam Coc Boat Trek and Village Cycling
experiences.description: Take a scenic sampan boat ride through the limestone karst caves of Tam Coc, then rent a bicycle to explore surrounding rice paddies and Bich Dong Pagoda. Stay in a guesthouse in Tam Coc village itself rather than in Ninh Binh city center to cut out the 9 km commute and start the boat trip early before crowds arrive. This is best scheduled mid-trip as a day trip from Hanoi or as an overnight stop.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Vietnam
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled - flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Noi Bai International Airport at 13:00. Take the 86 airport bus (~45 min, ~45,000 VND) to the Old Quarter. Check in to your boutique hostel, freshen up, and take a slow orientation walk around Hoan Kiem Lake (15-min walk from most Old Quarter guesthouses). Admire the Turtle Tower and Ngoc Son Temple from the lakeside path.
day_by_day.evening: Dive straight into the Old Quarter night scene. Explore the famous '36 Streets' on foot — each street historically named after the goods sold there. Head to Ta Hien Street ('Beer Street') for a cold Bia Hoi (fresh draft beer, ~5,000–10,000 VND per glass). Soak in the chaotic, vibrant atmosphere of your first Vietnamese night.

meals.breakfast: Eat on the plane or grab a snack at the airport
meals.lunch: Grab a Banh Mi sandwich from a street cart near the Old Quarter after check-in (~25,000–35,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Bun Cha (grilled pork with noodles) at a local street stall on Hang Manh or Ly Quoc Su Street (~50,000–70,000 VND)

day_by_day.notes: Exchange some USD to VND at the airport or at a gold shop in the Old Quarter for better rates. Avoid taxis from the airport — the 86 bus is safe, cheap, and reliable. Keep your bag close in the Old Quarter as it can be crowded.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early for a street food breakfast, then visit Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum Complex (free to enter the grounds, mausoleum entry ~40,000 VND). See the Presidential Palace, Ho Chi Minh's Stilt House, and the One Pillar Pagoda. Arrive before 10:00 to beat the crowds. The complex is about 3 km from the Old Quarter — take a Grab bike (~30,000 VND).
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to the Temple of Literature (Van Mieu) — Vietnam's first university, dating to 1070 (~30,000 VND entry). Spend 1.5 hours exploring the peaceful courtyards and stone steles. Afterward, visit Hoa Lo Prison ('Hanoi Hilton') nearby (~30,000 VND) for a sobering look at Vietnam's colonial and war history.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Old Quarter for the famous Hanoi Night Market on Hang Dao Street (open Friday–Sunday). Browse handicrafts, clothing, and souvenirs. Settle in at a plastic-stool street food spot on Ly Quoc Su or Hang Bong for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Pho Bo (beef noodle soup) from a sidewalk stall near your hostel (~40,000–60,000 VND) — look for places packed with locals
meals.lunch: Banh Cuon (steamed rice rolls) from a street vendor near Temple of Literature (~30,000–40,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Bun Bo Nam Bo (dry beef noodle salad) at a street restaurant in the Old Quarter (~50,000–70,000 VND) with a Bia Hoi on the side

day_by_day.notes: The mausoleum is closed on Mondays and Fridays and from September to November for annual maintenance — verify the schedule. Dress modestly (covered shoulders and knees) for the mausoleum and Temple of Literature.

day_by_day.date: Day 3 - April 17, 2027 (Hanoi Culture & Street Food Deep Dive)
day_by_day.morning: Join a free or low-cost walking tour of the Old Quarter (many hostels offer these or you can find free walking tour groups online). Visit the Bach Ma Temple, Dong Xuan Market (Hanoi's oldest and largest covered market), and the old city gate. A great way to understand the history of the '36 Streets'.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Vietnam Museum of Ethnology (~40,000 VND) — one of Southeast Asia's best ethnographic museums, showcasing the 54 ethnic groups of Vietnam. Take a Grab bike (~40,000 VND each way, about 5 km from the Old Quarter). Spend 2–3 hours here. On the way back, stop at West Lake (Ho Tay) and walk along the promenade.
day_by_day.evening: Take a Hoan Kiem Lake evening stroll and watch locals doing tai chi and aerobics. Then join a street food tour on foot — try Banh Goi (fried dumplings), Nem Chua Ran (fried fermented pork rolls), and Che (sweet dessert soup) from different vendors around the Old Quarter.

meals.breakfast: Xoi (sticky rice with toppings) from a street vendor — a classic Hanoi breakfast (~20,000–30,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Com Binh Dan (budget rice plate with multiple toppings) from a local canteen (~40,000–60,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Self-guided street food crawl around the Old Quarter — budget ~80,000–100,000 VND for multiple small dishes and snacks

day_by_day.notes: Dong Xuan Market is great for buying cheap souvenirs and local goods. Bargaining is expected — start at 50–60% of the asking price. The Vietnam Museum of Ethnology is well worth the entry fee and is less touristy than other Hanoi museums.

day_by_day.date: Day 4 - April 18, 2027 (Day Trip to Ninh Binh)
day_by_day.morning: Take an early bus from My Dinh or Giap Bat bus station to Ninh Binh (~2 hours, ~80,000–100,000 VND). Alternatively, book a budget day tour from the Old Quarter (~200,000–300,000 VND including transport). Arrive and rent a bicycle (~50,000 VND/day) to explore the area. Head to Trang An Grottoes — a UNESCO World Heritage site with stunning karst landscapes and cave-dotted waterways.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a 3-hour rowboat tour through Trang An (~200,000 VND per person) — boats are rowed by foot by local women through limestone caves and past rice paddies. Afterward, cycle to Bich Dong Pagoda, a beautiful cave pagoda carved into the mountainside (free entry).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Hanoi by bus or tour vehicle. Arrive back in the Old Quarter by 19:00–20:00. Relax with a cold Bia Hoi and reflect on the day's adventure.

meals.breakfast: Grab a Banh Mi or sticky rice from a street cart before the bus (~20,000–30,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Com Rang (fried rice) or grilled goat meat (a Ninh Binh specialty) at a local restaurant near Trang An (~60,000–80,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Back in Hanoi — Bun Cha or Pho at your favorite Old Quarter stall (~50,000–70,000 VND)

day_by_day.notes: Ninh Binh is often called 'Halong Bay on land' — absolutely worth the day trip. Book the Trang An boat tour (not Tam Coc) as it's longer and more scenic. Wear sunscreen and bring water. Start early to avoid midday heat.

day_by_day.morning: Check out of your Hanoi hostel. Take a Grab to Hanoi train station and board the Reunification Express train south to Hue (~14 hours, book a hard sleeper berth for ~350,000–500,000 VND for a budget-friendly overnight option — OR take a budget open-tour bus for ~200,000–250,000 VND, ~12–14 hours). If taking a daytime train or bus, enjoy the scenic countryside views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Settle in on the train or bus. The route through the Hai Van Pass (if taking the train) is one of the most scenic rail journeys in Southeast Asia. Watch rice paddies, fishing villages, and mountains roll by. Pack snacks and enjoy the journey.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive in Hue in the late evening (if taking overnight transport) or early evening (if flying — budget flights on VietJet/Bamboo from ~500,000 VND). Check in to a budget guesthouse in Hue's backpacker area near Pham Ngu Lao Street. Take a short walk along the Perfume River.

meals.breakfast: Pho or Banh Mi in Hanoi before departure (~40,000–50,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Train/bus snacks — pack instant noodles, bread, or fruit bought at Hanoi's Dong Xuan Market (~30,000–50,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Bun Bo Hue (Hue-style spicy beef noodle soup) at a local restaurant near your guesthouse (~40,000–60,000 VND) — a Hue specialty not to be missed

day_by_day.notes: Book train tickets at least 3–5 days in advance via the Vietnam Railways website or a hostel. The overnight sleeper is the most budget-friendly option and saves a night's accommodation. Store valuables in your daypack while sleeping on the train.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Imperial Citadel of Hue (~150,000 VND entry) — the former seat of the Nguyen Dynasty emperors. Spend 2–3 hours exploring the massive walled complex, the Forbidden Purple City, and the beautifully restored royal gates. Arrive early (08:00) to beat tour groups.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rent a bicycle (~50,000–80,000 VND/day) and cycle along the Perfume River to visit the Royal Tombs. The Tomb of Tu Duc is the most atmospheric and photogenic (~150,000 VND entry). Also visit Thien Mu Pagoda (free) — Hue's iconic 7-story pagoda overlooking the river, a 5-minute ride from Tu Duc.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Dong Ba Market for a street food dinner — Hue is famous for its royal cuisine and unique local dishes. Walk along the riverside promenade as the city lights up.

meals.breakfast: Banh Khoai (Hue-style crispy pancake) or Banh Beo (steamed rice cakes with shrimp) from a local street vendor (~30,000–50,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Com Hen (baby clam rice) — a Hue specialty sold from street carts (~30,000–40,000 VND)
meals.dinner: A spread of Hue royal dishes at Dong Ba Market — try Nem Lui (lemongrass pork skewers), Banh Nam, and Che desserts (~80,000–100,000 VND total)

day_by_day.notes: Hue's food is arguably Vietnam's most complex and flavorful regional cuisine — eat as much as possible here! The royal tombs are spread out — cycling is the best budget way to visit multiple sites. Hue can be rainy (it's one of Vietnam's wettest cities), so pack a light rain jacket.

day_by_day.date: Day 7 - April 21, 2027 (Travel to Hoi An via Hai Van Pass)
day_by_day.morning: Check out of your Hue guesthouse. Book a budget minibus or open-tour bus to Hoi An (~120,000–200,000 VND, ~3–4 hours) that crosses the legendary Hai Van Pass. The pass offers breathtaking views of the coastline and mountains — ask the driver to stop briefly at the top for photos. Alternatively, hire a motorbike taxi for a more thrilling experience (~300,000–400,000 VND).
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Hoi An by early afternoon. Check in to a budget guesthouse in the An Hoi area (across the river from the Ancient Town — cheaper than staying inside the old town). Walk across the Japanese Covered Bridge and explore the Ancient Town (~120,000 VND entry ticket, which includes 5 attraction entries).
day_by_day.evening: Experience Hoi An at its magical best — the Ancient Town glows with hundreds of silk lanterns after dark. Walk along the Thu Bon River, browse the lantern shops, and enjoy the romantic atmosphere. Thursday and Saturday evenings sometimes feature traditional music performances.

meals.breakfast: Grab a quick Banh Mi in Hue before departure (~25,000 VND)
meals.lunch: White Rose Dumplings (Banh Vac) and Cao Lau noodles at a local restaurant in Hoi An — both are Hoi An-exclusive dishes (~60,000–80,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Banh Mi Phuong — Hoi An's most famous banh mi stall (featured by Anthony Bourdain), located on Phan Chau Trinh Street (~35,000–45,000 VND). Pair with a fresh coconut (~20,000 VND)

day_by_day.notes: The Hoi An Ancient Town entry ticket is mandatory and covers 5 of 22 listed heritage sites. Buy it at any ticket booth around the old town. Hoi An is a great place to get custom clothes tailored cheaply — if interested, visit a tailor on Day 8 morning to allow time for fittings.

day_by_day.morning: Rent a bicycle (~50,000–80,000 VND/day) and cycle 4 km to An Bang Beach — a quieter, less commercialized beach than nearby Cua Dai. Swim, relax, and enjoy the South China Sea. Alternatively, cycle through the lush countryside villages surrounding Hoi An — the flat terrain makes it perfect for cycling.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the Ancient Town and visit the remaining heritage sites with your ticket: the Fujian Assembly Hall (stunning Chinese architecture), Tan Ky Old House, and the Museum of Trading Ceramics. Then browse the local market (Cho Hoi An) for fresh produce, spices, and cheap souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Join a budget cooking class (~300,000–400,000 VND) — many hostels and local families offer affordable versions that include a market visit, cooking session, and eating your creations. This is one of the best cultural experiences in Vietnam. Book through your guesthouse.

meals.breakfast: Mi Quang (Hoi An-style turmeric noodles with pork and shrimp) at a local market stall (~40,000–50,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood grilled at a beachside shack at An Bang Beach (~100,000–150,000 VND for a full plate of grilled fish or prawns)
meals.dinner: Eat the dishes you cooked in your cooking class, or grab Com Ga (Hoi An chicken rice) from a street stall (~40,000–60,000 VND)

day_by_day.notes: Hoi An is extremely walkable and bikeable — you won't need taxis or Grab much here. The town gets very crowded midday with day-trippers from Da Nang; mornings and evenings are the best times to explore. If getting clothes tailored, do a fitting today.

day_by_day.date: Day 9 - April 23, 2027 (Travel to Ho Chi Minh City)
day_by_day.morning: Check out of your Hoi An guesthouse. Take a shuttle to Da Nang Airport (~50,000–80,000 VND, 30 min). Catch a budget flight to Ho Chi Minh City (Saigon) with VietJet, Bamboo, or Vietravel Airlines (~400,000–700,000 VND, booked in advance). Flight time is ~1.5 hours. Arrive at Tan Son Nhat Airport by midday.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take bus 109 from the airport to Ben Thanh Market area (~6,000 VND — the cheapest airport transfer in Vietnam). Check in to a budget hostel in the Pham Ngu Lao backpacker district. Explore the Ben Thanh Market area and the surrounding streets. Visit the Reunification Palace (~40,000 VND) — frozen in time from April 30, 1975.
day_by_day.evening: Walk to Bui Vien Street — HCMC's famous backpacker street — for a lively, chaotic, neon-lit evening. Have a beer, meet fellow travelers, and soak in the energy of Vietnam's most dynamic city.

meals.breakfast: Banh Mi or Xoi from a street vendor in Hoi An before the shuttle (~25,000–35,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Grab a quick Com Tam (broken rice with grilled pork) near Ben Thanh Market after arriving (~50,000–70,000 VND) — this is HCMC's signature dish
meals.dinner: Pho or Hu Tieu (Southern-style noodle soup) from a street cart on Pham Ngu Lao Street (~50,000–60,000 VND)

day_by_day.notes: Book the Da Nang to HCMC flight well in advance for the best budget prices. Avoid metered taxis at HCMC airport — use the official airport bus or pre-book a Grab. The Pham Ngu Lao district is the best budget base in HCMC with cheap dorms, street food, and easy access to sights.

day_by_day.date: Day 10 - April 24, 2027 (Ho Chi Minh City - Final Day)
day_by_day.morning: Visit the War Remnants Museum (~40,000 VND) — one of the most powerful and moving museums in Southeast Asia, documenting the Vietnam War from the Vietnamese perspective. Allow 2 hours. Nearby, visit the Notre-Dame Cathedral de Saigon and the historic Central Post Office (free to enter) — both stunning French colonial landmarks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore District 1's street art scene and the vibrant local neighborhoods. Visit the Jade Emperor Pagoda (free) — an atmospheric Taoist temple with incense-filled halls and intricate carvings. Then head to the Saigon Skydeck at Bitexco Financial Tower (~200,000 VND) for panoramic views of the city — a splurge worth considering on your last day.
day_by_day.evening: Final street food farewell dinner — head to a local Com Tam restaurant or the night market near Ben Thanh for one last spread of Vietnamese food. Raise a final Bia Saigon (~15,000–20,000 VND) to an incredible 10-day journey through Vietnam.

meals.breakfast: Banh Mi Op La (banh mi with fried eggs) from a street cart near your hostel (~25,000–35,000 VND) — a classic HCMC breakfast
meals.lunch: Com Tam Suon Bi Cha (broken rice with grilled pork ribs, shredded pork skin, and steamed egg) at a local Com Tam restaurant (~60,000–80,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Grand finale street food feast — Goi Cuon (fresh spring rolls), Banh Xeo (sizzling crepes), and Che dessert at a local restaurant or night market (~100,000–150,000 VND for a full spread)

day_by_day.notes: If departing from HCMC, allow at least 3 hours before your flight for the taxi/Grab ride to Tan Son Nhat Airport (traffic can be severe). The Cu Chi Tunnels (45 km from HCMC, ~150,000 VND entry + ~150,000 VND transport) can be substituted for the afternoon if you prefer a half-day excursion outside the city. Overall 10-day budget estimate: ~4,000,000–6,000,000 VND (~$160–$240 USD) excluding flights.

trip_options.title: Classic Vietnam Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Hanoi Noi Bai Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Take a taxi or airport bus (Bus 86) to your boutique hotel in the Old Quarter. Check in, freshen up, and get oriented with a quick rest.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a leisurely stroll around Hoan Kiem Lake, just a short walk from the Old Quarter. Visit Ngoc Son Temple on the lake island (small entrance fee ~30,000 VND). Walk across the iconic red Huc Bridge and soak in the atmosphere of the surrounding park.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the famous Hanoi Night Market on Hang Dao Street (open Friday–Sunday) or wander the lantern-lit alleyways of the Old Quarter. Browse local crafts, street snacks, and enjoy the buzzing energy of your first Vietnamese night.

meals.breakfast: Skip or grab a light snack at the airport before landing.
meals.lunch: Bun Cha Huong Lien (Hang Manh St) — a legendary spot for bun cha (grilled pork with noodles), ~60,000–80,000 VND per person.
meals.dinner: Cha Ca Thang Long on Duong Thanh Street — try the iconic Hanoi turmeric fish dish (cha ca), ~150,000–200,000 VND per person.

day_by_day.notes: Exchange some USD to VND at the airport or a local exchange bureau in the Old Quarter. Keep small bills handy for street food. Jet lag tip: stay awake until at least 9 PM local time to adjust faster.

day_by_day.morning: Start with a bowl of pho at a classic Old Quarter street stall, then visit Hoa Lo Prison (Hanoi Hilton) for a powerful historical experience (~30,000 VND entry). Afterward, walk to the Temple of Literature — Vietnam's first university, a stunning example of traditional Vietnamese architecture (~30,000 VND entry).
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Vietnam Museum of Ethnology (~40,000 VND) to explore the rich cultural diversity of Vietnam's 54 ethnic groups. Exhibits are well-curated and bilingual. Spend 2–3 hours here. Return to the Old Quarter via grab bike or taxi.
day_by_day.evening: Join a free or low-cost walking tour of the Old Quarter's 36 ancient guild streets. Each street is named after the trade historically practiced there (Hang Bac = silver, Hang Gai = silk). End the night at a bia hoi (street beer) corner — try the famous Bia Hoi Junction at the intersection of Luong Ngoc Quyen and Ta Hien Streets.

meals.breakfast: Pho Thin on Lo Duc Street or a local pho stall near your hotel — ~40,000–60,000 VND.
meals.lunch: Banh Mi 25 on Hang Ca Street — one of Hanoi's best banh mi spots, ~35,000–50,000 VND.
meals.dinner: Quan An Ngon on Phan Boi Chau Street — a courtyard restaurant serving a wide variety of Vietnamese street food classics in a comfortable setting, ~100,000–180,000 VND per person.

day_by_day.notes: The Temple of Literature is most photogenic in the morning light. Wear modest clothing as it is a place of cultural reverence. Grab bikes (via the Grab app) are the most efficient and affordable way to get around Hanoi.

day_by_day.morning: Take an early morning bus or booked minivan to Ha Long Bay (approximately 3.5–4 hours). Arrive at the harbor and board a mid-range overnight cruise (book in advance — recommended operators include Bhaya Cruises or Paradise Sails for mid-range options, ~$80–$130 USD/night including meals). Set sail and enjoy the dramatic karst limestone scenery.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cruise through the emerald waters of Ha Long Bay. Stop at a floating fishing village (Vung Vieng or Cua Van) to kayak or take a bamboo boat tour through the village (~included with most cruises). Explore hidden lagoons and limestone caves.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a sunset on the cruise deck with drinks. Participate in a cooking demonstration on board, followed by a fresh seafood dinner. Squid fishing from the boat deck is often offered after dinner.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at the hotel or grab banh mi on the way to the bus station.
meals.lunch: Served on board the cruise — typically fresh Vietnamese dishes with seafood.
meals.dinner: Full dinner on board the cruise — fresh seafood, spring rolls, stir-fried vegetables, and rice.

day_by_day.notes: Book your Ha Long Bay cruise at least 1–2 weeks in advance. Pack light for the cruise — leave heavy bags at your Hanoi hotel (most boutique stays offer luggage storage). Bring sunscreen, a light rain jacket, and motion sickness tablets just in case.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early for a sunrise on the bay deck — truly spectacular. Enjoy a tai chi session offered on most cruise decks. After breakfast, visit Sung Sot Cave (Surprising Cave) — one of the largest and most impressive grottos in Ha Long Bay (usually included in cruise itinerary).
day_by_day.afternoon: Disembark the cruise around 12:00–13:00 and take the return bus/minivan back to Hanoi (arriving ~17:00). Check back into your Old Quarter hotel and rest.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a traditional Water Puppet Show at Thang Long Water Puppet Theatre near Hoan Kiem Lake (~100,000 VND). This uniquely Vietnamese art form dates back to the 11th century and is not to be missed. Book tickets in advance as shows sell out.

meals.breakfast: Included on the cruise — Vietnamese breakfast spread with pho, eggs, fruit, and bread.
meals.lunch: Light meal on the cruise before disembarkation or a quick stop en route back to Hanoi.
meals.dinner: Xoi Yen on Nguyen Huu Huan Street — famous sticky rice shop with various toppings, ~40,000–70,000 VND. Light, affordable, and delicious.

day_by_day.notes: The return journey from Ha Long can be tiring. Consider booking a sleeper bus for added comfort if you prefer. Keep your energy up — you have an early train or bus the next day heading south.

day_by_day.morning: Take an early morning flight or overnight train (book in advance) from Hanoi to Da Nang or Hue. If flying (recommended for time efficiency — ~1.5 hours, ~$30–$60 USD on VietJet or Bamboo Airways), arrive in Da Nang by mid-morning. Transfer to Hue by taxi or grab (~1.5 hours, ~$20–$30 USD) or local bus.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check into a mid-range guesthouse in Hue's city center. After settling in, visit the Imperial Citadel of Hue — the former seat of the Nguyen Dynasty emperors (~200,000 VND entry). Spend 2–3 hours exploring the grand gates, pavilions, and royal gardens.
day_by_day.evening: Walk along the Perfume River promenade at sunset. Cross the Truong Tien Bridge for great views. Explore the vibrant Dong Ba Market for local crafts and street snacks.

meals.breakfast: Grab a quick banh mi or xoi (sticky rice) near your Old Quarter hotel before heading to the airport.
meals.lunch: Bun Bo Hue at a local stall near the citadel — Hue's signature spicy beef noodle soup, ~40,000–60,000 VND.
meals.dinner: Hanh Restaurant on Doi Cung Street — a beloved local spot for authentic Hue royal cuisine, ~100,000–160,000 VND per person. Try banh khoai (crispy pancakes) and com hen (rice with baby clams).

day_by_day.notes: Hue is considered the culinary capital of Vietnam — be adventurous with local dishes. The city is best explored by bicycle (rentable for ~50,000–80,000 VND/day) or by motorbike taxi. Weather in April is generally warm but can have brief rain showers.

day_by_day.morning: Rent a bicycle or hire a motorbike driver to explore Hue's royal tombs. Visit the Tomb of Tu Duc (~100,000 VND) — the most romantic and picturesque of all the tombs, surrounded by lotus ponds and pine trees. Then visit the Tomb of Khai Dinh (~100,000 VND) — a striking fusion of Vietnamese and European architecture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Thien Mu Pagoda — Hue's most iconic religious landmark perched on a hill above the Perfume River (free entry). Take a dragon boat ride along the Perfume River back to the city center (~150,000–200,000 VND per boat, shareable with other travelers). Stop at a local incense-making village along the river.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Hue's street food scene on a self-guided walking tour. Try as many local specialties as possible from street vendors around the Dong Ba Market area.

meals.breakfast: Banh Mi Phuong or a local bakery near your guesthouse — ~25,000–40,000 VND.
meals.lunch: Com Hen (baby clam rice) at a roadside stall near the Perfume River — ~30,000–50,000 VND. A true Hue specialty.
meals.dinner: Street food crawl: try nem lui (grilled pork skewers with rice paper), banh beo (steamed rice cakes), and banh nam (flat steamed rice dumplings) from street vendors, ~60,000–100,000 VND total.

day_by_day.notes: A combo ticket for multiple royal tombs is available and offers better value. Start early to beat the midday heat. The dragon boat ride is a wonderful way to see the river and pagoda — negotiate the price before boarding.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Hue early and take the scenic Hai Van Pass road to Hoi An (hire a motorbike driver or join a group tour, ~$20–$35 USD). Stop at the top of Hai Van Pass for breathtaking coastal panoramas — one of the most dramatic viewpoints in Southeast Asia. This route was famously featured on Top Gear.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Hoi An and check into a mid-range boutique hotel in or near the Ancient Town. Explore the UNESCO-listed Ancient Town on foot — visit the iconic Japanese Covered Bridge (free to view, ~120,000 VND for an Old Town ticket covering 5 monuments), Chinese Assembly Halls, and colonial-era merchant houses.
day_by_day.evening: Wander the Ancient Town at night when it transforms into a magical lantern-lit wonderland. Release a paper lantern on the Thu Bon River (~20,000–30,000 VND). Browse the night market for silk lanterns, tailored clothing, and souvenirs.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at your Hue guesthouse before departure.
meals.lunch: White Rose Restaurant (Quan Com Hoi An) — famous for Hoi An's signature white rose dumplings and fried wontons, ~80,000–120,000 VND.
meals.dinner: Banh Mi Phuong on Phan Chau Trinh Street — arguably the most famous banh mi in Vietnam (endorsed by Anthony Bourdain), ~35,000–50,000 VND. Follow with a sit-down meal at Morning Glory Restaurant for cao lau (Hoi An pork noodles), ~100,000–160,000 VND.

day_by_day.notes: The Hai Van Pass road trip is one of the highlights of any Vietnam trip — do not skip it if weather permits. Hoi An's Ancient Town is best explored on foot. The Old Town ticket is required to enter specific monuments but general walking and browsing is free.

day_by_day.morning: Rent a bicycle (~80,000–100,000 VND/day) and cycle to An Bang Beach or Cua Dai Beach (approximately 4–5 km from the Ancient Town). Spend the morning swimming and relaxing on the beach. Hoi An's beaches are less crowded than Da Nang's and have a more laid-back atmosphere.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to town and visit the Hoi An Central Market — a lively wet market perfect for street food exploration. Sign up for a half-day Vietnamese cooking class (many options available, ~$20–$35 USD, includes a market tour, cooking session, and meal). This is one of the best cultural experiences in Vietnam.
day_by_day.evening: Get measured and fitted at one of Hoi An's famous tailor shops (the town is renowned for custom-made clothing at affordable prices — allow 24–48 hours for tailoring). Stroll the riverfront, enjoy a cocktail at a rooftop bar, and watch the lanterns reflect on the Thu Bon River.

meals.breakfast: Banh Cuon (steamed rice rolls) from a street stall in the Ancient Town — ~30,000–50,000 VND.
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood at a beachside shack at An Bang Beach — grilled fish, prawns, and cold beer, ~100,000–180,000 VND.
meals.dinner: Eat what you cooked in your cooking class, or visit Cargo Club Restaurant on Nguyen Thai Hoc Street for a fusion Vietnamese-Western menu with river views, ~120,000–200,000 VND per person.

day_by_day.notes: Book your cooking class in advance — Red Bridge Cooking School and Hoi An Eco Cooking Class are highly rated mid-range options. If you want tailored clothes, visit the tailor today so they're ready before you leave. Recommended tailor: Yaly Couture or Bebe Tailor.

day_by_day.morning: Take an early flight from Da Nang to Ho Chi Minh City (Saigon) — approximately 1.5 hours (~$25–$50 USD on budget airlines). Transfer from Tan Son Nhat Airport to your accommodation in District 1 or the Backpacker District (Pham Ngu Lao area). Check in and drop your bags.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the War Remnants Museum (~40,000 VND) — a sobering and essential historical experience documenting the Vietnam War from the Vietnamese perspective. Afterward, explore the nearby Reunification Palace (~40,000 VND), the historic site where the Vietnam War officially ended on April 30, 1975.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Ben Thanh Market for a street food dinner in the outdoor night market surrounding the main building. This is one of the best spots in Saigon for affordable, diverse Vietnamese street food. Afterward, explore the neon-lit streets of District 1 and the rooftop bar scene.

meals.breakfast: Grab airport food or eat at your Hoi An hotel before departure.
meals.lunch: Bun Thit Nuong (grilled pork vermicelli) at a local stall near the War Remnants Museum — ~40,000–60,000 VND.
meals.dinner: Ben Thanh Night Market street food — try banh xeo (sizzling crepes), goi cuon (fresh spring rolls), and che (Vietnamese sweet dessert soup), ~80,000–150,000 VND total.

day_by_day.notes: Ho Chi Minh City is fast-paced and energetic — very different from Hanoi and Hoi An. Use Grab for all transportation as metered taxis can sometimes overcharge tourists. Keep your belongings secure, especially on busy streets.

day_by_day.morning: Take a half-day trip to the Cu Chi Tunnels (~70 km from HCMC, ~$15–$25 USD for a guided group tour including transport). Explore the vast underground tunnel network used by Viet Cong soldiers during the war. Crawl through the tunnels, see booby traps, and learn about guerrilla warfare tactics. A truly unforgettable experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Ho Chi Minh City by early afternoon. Visit the Notre-Dame Cathedral of Saigon and the adjacent Central Post Office — a stunning French colonial building still in operation. Walk along Dong Khoi Street and browse the shops and cafes. Visit the Fine Arts Museum (~30,000 VND) housed in a beautiful colonial villa.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Vietnam — celebrate with a special dinner and explore the city's vibrant nightlife. Visit the rooftop bar at the Chill Sky Bar (Level 26, AB Tower) for panoramic views of the Saigon skyline. End the night with a walk through the Bui Vien Walking Street — the heart of Saigon's backpacker scene, full of live music, street food, and energy.

meals.breakfast: Banh Mi from a street cart near your hotel — ~25,000–40,000 VND. Quick and perfect before the early tour departure.
meals.lunch: Pho Hoa Pasteur on Pasteur Street — one of Saigon's most famous pho restaurants, open since 1960, ~60,000–90,000 VND.
meals.dinner: Nha Hang Ngon on Nam Ky Khoi Nghia Street — a beautiful garden restaurant serving dishes from all regions of Vietnam, ~120,000–200,000 VND per person. Perfect for a memorable farewell dinner.

day_by_day.notes: Book the Cu Chi Tunnels tour the evening before to secure your spot. For your departure, allow at least 3 hours before your flight for Tan Son Nhat Airport, as traffic in HCMC can be unpredictable. Consider keeping a small amount of VND for last-minute snacks or transport to the airport.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Vietnam Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Noi Bai International Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Private luxury transfer arranged from airport to Boutique Stay in Old Quarter, Hanoi (approximately 45–60 minutes). Check-in, freshen up, and settle into your accommodation.
day_by_day.afternoon: Gentle orientation walk through the iconic 36 Streets of Hanoi's Old Quarter. Explore the labyrinthine alleyways, browse artisan shops selling silk, lacquerware, and handicrafts. Visit Hoan Kiem Lake and the red-painted Huc Bridge leading to Ngoc Son Temple — a serene cultural introduction to the city.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the Hoan Kiem Lake promenade as it comes alive at dusk. Experience the famous Hanoi Weekend Night Market (or evening street scene on Hang Dao Street). Enjoy a welcome cocktail at a rooftop bar overlooking the Old Quarter.

meals.breakfast: N/A — mid-day arrival
meals.lunch: Light welcome meal at Cha Ca Thang Long — a heritage restaurant renowned for its signature turmeric-marinated grilled fish (Cha Ca La Vong), a Hanoi culinary institution.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Ly Club — a refined French-Vietnamese restaurant set in a stunning colonial villa, offering elevated Vietnamese cuisine with premium wine pairings.

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 begins post-arrival at 13:00. Keep the pace relaxed to recover from travel. Ensure private airport transfer is pre-booked. April in Hanoi is warm (26–32°C) with occasional light showers — pack a light layer.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum Complex — explore the Presidential Palace gardens, Ho Chi Minh's Stilt House, and the One Pillar Pagoda. Afterward, walk to the Temple of Literature (Van Mieu), Vietnam's first university dating to 1070, for a deep dive into Confucian heritage and classical Vietnamese architecture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Vietnam Museum of Ethnology — one of Southeast Asia's finest museums, showcasing the cultures of Vietnam's 54 ethnic groups through immersive exhibits, traditional costumes, and reconstructed village houses. Hire a private guide for an enriched experience. Return to the Old Quarter for a premium Vietnamese coffee experience at Cafe Giang, the birthplace of Hanoi's famous egg coffee.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a traditional Water Puppet Show at the Thang Long Water Puppet Theatre — a uniquely Vietnamese art form dating back to the 11th century. Post-show, enjoy an evening exploring the vibrant street food scene around Hang Be Market.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel or at Pho Thin — a legendary Old Quarter pho shop serving Hanoi's most celebrated beef noodle soup since 1979.
meals.lunch: Lunch at KOTO (Know One Teach One) — a premium social enterprise restaurant offering refined Vietnamese dishes in a beautiful setting near the Temple of Literature.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Chim Sao — an acclaimed restaurant specializing in authentic northern Vietnamese cuisine and dishes from ethnic minority communities, with a warm, rustic-chic ambiance.

day_by_day.notes: Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum is closed on Mondays and Fridays, and only open in the mornings (7:30–10:30). Verify the day of the week and adjust if needed. Dress modestly for temple and mausoleum visits.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day premium excursion to Ninh Binh (approximately 2 hours from Hanoi by private car). Morning visit to Trang An Landscape Complex — a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Take a private rowing boat through dramatic limestone karsts, hidden caves, and emerald waterways. Visit ancient temples and pagodas along the route.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hike or take a cable car up to Bich Dong Pagoda, carved into a limestone cliff. Explore the ancient capital of Hoa Lu — Vietnam's 10th-century royal capital — visiting the Dinh and Le Dynasty temples. Enjoy the lush rural countryside scenery.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Hanoi by private car. Relax and freshen up at the hotel before a leisurely evening in the Old Quarter.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel before departure.
meals.lunch: Lunch at a premium riverside restaurant in Ninh Binh — try local specialties including goat meat (de nuong), burnt rice (com chay), and freshwater fish from the Ngo Dong River.
meals.dinner: Dinner at La Badiane — a celebrated Hanoi restaurant offering creative French-Vietnamese fusion cuisine in a beautiful colonial courtyard setting.

day_by_day.notes: Depart early (around 7:30–8:00 AM) to maximize time at Ninh Binh. Wear comfortable walking shoes and bring sun protection. The boat ride at Trang An takes approximately 2–3 hours. Pre-book a private boat for a more exclusive experience.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Hanoi for Ha Long Bay by private luxury transfer (approximately 3.5 hours). Board a premium overnight cruise — choose a vessel from Indochine Cruise, Paradise Elegance, or Signature Halong for a truly luxurious experience. Morning welcome aboard with champagne, followed by a scenic sailing through the UNESCO-listed bay of 1,969 limestone islands.
day_by_day.afternoon: Kayaking or bamboo boat excursion through hidden lagoons and sea caves (Luon Cave or Dark & Bright Cave). Swimming in the emerald waters of a secluded cove. Onboard cooking class learning to prepare Vietnamese spring rolls and fresh seafood dishes.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails on the sundeck as the cruise anchors in a private bay. Squid fishing off the deck under a canopy of stars. Premium seafood dinner prepared by the onboard chef.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel before departure.
meals.lunch: Welcome lunch aboard the cruise — fresh seafood including grilled prawns, steamed clams, and local fish with Vietnamese dipping sauces.
meals.dinner: Formal onboard dinner — multi-course Vietnamese and international menu featuring lobster, crab, and seasonal seafood paired with premium wines.

day_by_day.notes: Pack an overnight bag for the cruise (2 nights recommended). Bring swimwear, sunscreen, and a light jacket for evenings on the water. April weather in Ha Long Bay is generally warm and pleasant with calm seas — ideal cruising conditions.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning Tai Chi session on the sundeck at sunrise. Kayak or boat excursion to Vung Vieng Fishing Village — a floating community in the heart of Ha Long Bay. Explore the village by kayak, meet local fishermen, and learn about traditional aquaculture. Visit Surprise Cave (Hang Sung Sot) — one of Ha Long Bay's most spectacular grottos.
day_by_day.afternoon: Leisurely afternoon cruising through the bay. Sunbathing on deck, spa treatments (massage or body scrub available on premium vessels), and swimming. The cruise begins its return journey toward the harbor.
day_by_day.evening: Disembark at Ha Long pier and transfer back to Hanoi by private car. Evening at leisure in the Old Quarter — explore the night scene or enjoy a quiet evening at the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Full Vietnamese and Western breakfast aboard the cruise at sunrise.
meals.lunch: Final onboard lunch — light Vietnamese dishes including fresh spring rolls, pho, and tropical fruits before disembarkation.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Bun Cha Huong Lien — the legendary Hanoi restaurant made world-famous by Anthony Bourdain and Barack Obama's visit, serving classic bun cha (grilled pork with vermicelli noodles).

day_by_day.notes: Disembarkation is typically around 11:00–12:00. The drive back to Hanoi takes approximately 3.5 hours. Consider an optional stop at a local lacquerware or ceramics workshop in Quang Ninh Province on the way back.

day_by_day.morning: Fly from Hanoi (HAN) to Da Nang (DAD) — approximately 1.5-hour flight. Private luxury transfer to your premium hotel in Hoi An Ancient Town (approximately 30 minutes from Da Nang airport). Check in and freshen up. Morning stroll through the UNESCO World Heritage-listed Hoi An Ancient Town — admire the remarkably preserved trading port architecture, Japanese Covered Bridge, and colorful lantern-draped streets.
day_by_day.afternoon: Guided cultural tour of Hoi An's heritage houses — visit the Tan Ky Ancient House (200-year-old merchant home), Phuc Kien Assembly Hall (Chinese community temple), and the Museum of Trade Ceramics. Visit a premium tailor shop on Le Loi Street for bespoke Vietnamese clothing — Hoi An is renowned worldwide for its skilled tailors.
day_by_day.evening: Join a lantern-making workshop at a local craft studio — a quintessential Hoi An cultural experience. Release a lantern on the Thu Bon River at dusk. Explore the magical lantern-lit streets of the Ancient Town after dark.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel before departure or grab a banh mi from one of Hanoi's legendary street stalls.
meals.lunch: Lunch at White Rose Restaurant (Hoi An) — the exclusive home of Hoi An's iconic white rose dumplings and crispy wontons, a local culinary treasure.
meals.dinner: Dinner at The Field Restaurant — an acclaimed Hoi An restaurant set amid rice paddies, offering refined Central Vietnamese cuisine with stunning rural views and lantern ambiance.

day_by_day.notes: Book flights from Hanoi to Da Nang in advance. Hoi An's Ancient Town is best explored on foot or by bicycle. April is a good time to visit — warm weather before the rainy season. The tailor visit is best done today to allow time for fittings over the next day.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise bicycle ride through Hoi An's countryside — cycle through rice paddies, water buffalo fields, and traditional villages to the Thu Bon River. Take a basket boat (thung chai) ride with local fishermen — a unique circular woven bamboo boat experience. Visit Tra Que Vegetable Village, an organic farming community, and participate in a hands-on farming and cooking experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to the Marble Mountains (Ngu Hanh Son) near Da Nang — a cluster of five marble and limestone hills housing Buddhist sanctuaries, pagodas, and caves. Climb to panoramic viewpoints over Da Nang Bay. Continue to My Khe Beach (Da Nang) for a relaxing afternoon swim and sunbathing at one of Asia's most beautiful beaches.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Hoi An. Tailor fitting appointment. Evening at leisure exploring the Ancient Town's boutique shops, art galleries, and silk stores.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel — or try Banh Mi Phuong on Phan Chau Trinh Street, widely regarded as Vietnam's finest banh mi shop.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Mango Mango Restaurant — a stylish riverside restaurant in Hoi An offering creative Vietnamese and fusion cuisine with beautiful river views.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Cargo Club Restaurant — a beloved Hoi An institution offering Vietnamese and international cuisine across two floors with a stunning riverside terrace.

day_by_day.notes: The basket boat experience is highly photogenic and culturally unique — confirm booking in advance. Marble Mountains requires moderate walking/climbing — wear comfortable shoes. Sunset from the Marble Mountains is spectacular if timing allows.

day_by_day.morning: Morning flight or private car transfer from Da Nang to Ho Chi Minh City (Saigon) — approximately 1.5-hour flight. Private luxury transfer to your premium hotel in District 1, the heart of Saigon. Check in and freshen up. Begin exploring the French colonial heart of Ho Chi Minh City — visit Notre-Dame Cathedral Basilica of Saigon, the Central Post Office (designed by Gustave Eiffel), and the historic Opera House.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the War Remnants Museum — a powerful and sobering museum documenting the Vietnam War, essential for understanding modern Vietnamese history. Explore the vibrant Ben Thanh Market area for street food and local crafts. Take a premium cyclo (rickshaw) tour through the French Quarter's tree-lined boulevards and colonial architecture.
day_by_day.evening: Rooftop cocktails at Chill Skybar (AB Tower) or EON Heli Bar — among Saigon's most spectacular rooftop bars with panoramic city views. Explore the electric nightlife and street food scene of Bui Vien Walking Street.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel or at a Hoi An café before departure.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Nha Hang Ngon (Saigon) — a stunning colonial villa setting showcasing street food stalls from across Vietnam's regions in an upscale, curated environment.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Cuc Gach Quan — one of Saigon's most celebrated restaurants, set in a beautifully restored colonial house, serving authentic home-style Vietnamese cuisine beloved by locals and discerning travelers alike.

day_by_day.notes: Ho Chi Minh City is significantly hotter than Hanoi (30–35°C in April). Stay hydrated and wear light, breathable clothing. District 1 is walkable for most major attractions. The War Remnants Museum can be emotionally intense — allow sufficient time and emotional space.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day Mekong Delta premium excursion departing from Ho Chi Minh City (approximately 2 hours by private car to My Tho or Ben Tre). Board a private boat for an immersive journey through the Mekong River's labyrinthine waterways, coconut palm-lined canals, and floating markets. Visit a coconut candy workshop, honey bee farm, and rice paper production facility.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the floating markets (Cai Rang or Cai Be) by private sampan boat — witness the unique river trading culture of the Mekong Delta. Cycle through rural villages on elevated dikes between rice paddies and orchards. Visit a local family home for an authentic homestay-style lunch experience.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Ho Chi Minh City by private car. Final evening in Saigon — explore the chic Thao Dien neighborhood in District 2 or the trendy Nguyen Van Binh Book Street.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel before departure.
meals.lunch: Authentic Mekong Delta lunch at a local family's riverside home — fresh elephant ear fish (ca tai tuong) grilled tableside, river prawns, and tropical fruits from the delta orchards.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Quince Saigon — a sophisticated rooftop restaurant in the heart of District 1 offering modern Vietnamese and international cuisine with stunning city panoramas and an exceptional wine list.

day_by_day.notes: Depart early (7:00–7:30 AM) to reach the Mekong Delta before the heat peaks. Wear comfortable, light clothing and bring insect repellent. A premium Mekong tour operator (Les Rives Experience or Mekong Eyes Cruise) is highly recommended for a luxury experience.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Ho Chi Minh City. Visit the Jade Emperor Pagoda (Phuoc Hai Tu) — one of Saigon's most atmospheric and ornate Taoist temples, a hidden gem away from the tourist crowds. Stroll through the charming antique shops and art galleries of Nguyen Hue Walking Boulevard. Last-minute premium souvenir shopping — Vietnamese lacquerware, silk scarves, Phu Quoc pepper, and artisan coffee at high-end boutiques.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of the hotel. Leisurely lunch before private luxury transfer to Tan Son Nhat International Airport (SGN) for departure. Allow 2.5–3 hours before your flight for check-in and security at the international terminal.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Ho Chi Minh City. Reflect on an extraordinary 10-day journey through Vietnam's cultural, culinary, and natural wonders.

meals.breakfast: Final Vietnamese breakfast — try a bowl of hu tieu (Saigon-style pork and seafood noodle soup) from a renowned local spot such as Hu Tieu Nam Vang on Vo Van Tan Street.
meals.lunch: Farewell lunch at The Refinery — a stylish restaurant in a beautifully restored French colonial opium refinery, offering French-Vietnamese cuisine in one of Saigon's most atmospheric heritage settings.
meals.dinner: Airport lounge dining or in-flight meal depending on departure time.

day_by_day.notes: Confirm departure flight time and adjust the Day 10 schedule accordingly. Allow ample time for airport transfer — Saigon traffic can be unpredictable. Consider booking access to the premium lounge at Tan Son Nhat Airport for a comfortable pre-departure experience. Ensure all tailor-made items from Hoi An have been collected or shipped.
